articles.title: Yankees let pitcher Luis Gil go, declining to tender contract 2 seasons after winning AL Rookie of the Year
articles.summary: Gil had been injured throughout the past two seasons and struggled with walks while pitching in relief.
articles.body:
Two years after Luis Gil won American League Rookie of the Year honors , the New York Yankees decided not to tender a contract to the right-hander, making him a free agent.

The decision came before Friday's 5 p.m. ET deadline for offering contracts to players still under club control.

Gil compiled a 3.50 ERA, a 15-7 record and 171 strikeouts in 151 1/3 innings during the 2024 season, looking like a part of the Yankees' starting rotation for years to come.

However, he suffered a high-grade right lat strain during spring training the following season. That sidelined Gil until August. He was effective upon his return, compiling a 3.32 ERA in 11 starts, but his strikeout rate dropped from 10.1 batters per nine innings to 6.5.

This past season, Gil struggled during spring training and was not part of the Yankees' opening day starting rotation .

He joined the major-league roster in April, but registered a 6.05 ERA in four starts (allowing 13 runs in 19 1/3 innings) and was demoted back to Triple-A. While with Scranton/Wilkes-Barre, Gil was placed on the injured list with shoulder inflammation and shut down for three months.

Called up just before September, Gil worked out of the bullpen and compiled a 4.61 ERA in five appearances. However, control was a major issue — as it was throughout his Yankees career — with seven walks in eight innings. Ultimately, he was assigned to the Yankees' Florida rookie league affiliate in late September and left off their postseason roster.

Gil, 28, was set for his first year of arbitration eligibility next spring.

The Yankees also non-tendered reliever Fernando Cruz. The 36-year-old right-hander made 61 appearances, striking out 67 batters in 54 2/3 innings. But he sustained a partially torn ulnar collateral ligament in late August, ending his season.

Cruz was acquired before the 2025 season from the Cincinnati Reds in a trade for catcher Jose Trevino. He was one of the Yankees' most effective relievers, notching 72 strikeouts in 48 innings.

articles.title: Giants make major change in stance on Logan Webb trade rumors
articles.summary: This is a surprising update for the Giants on the potential of a Logan Webb trade.
articles.body:
The San Francisco Giants sold off a few key players at the MLB trade deadline this past season, but they didn't move any core players signed to long-term deals.

That could change this offseason, with Rafael Devers, Matt Chapman, and Willy Adames as names to watch who could be on the move. However, a new name has emerged as one this Giants team is willing to listen to offers for: Logan Webb.

According to MLB insider Robert Murray of Fansided.com , the Giants have taken a major change in stance on the Webb trade rumors, as they're now open to offers for the star right-hander this offseason.

Giants open to trade offers for Logan Webb

"For years, the San Francisco Giants refused to engage or listen to any inquiries involving star right-handed pitcher Logan Webb. That is no longer the case," Murray reports. "The Giants are open to listening to offers for Webb, multiple rival executives say."

This is a huge change in stance from the Giants, as they've been steadfast in recent years that Webb isn't going anywhere. They shut down trade offers for him at this past MLB trade deadline.

The 30-year-old right-hander would fetch a huge return if traded, and now it appears the Giants are open to a trade, as they're listening to offers for Webb.

He might not actually be traded this offseason, or ever, by the Giants. But their willingness to listen to trade inquiries is still a major shift in philosophy for the Giants.

Webb is signed for the next two seasons on his five-year, $90 million deal. There are bound to be plenty of teams willing to make a push to acquire Webb.

Teams that miss out on Tarik Skubal and some of the other top free agent starters might turn to the Giants for a Webb trade.

Before, the Giants would turn down all offers. Now, they're open to a deal, as they're reportedly going to listen to trade offers for Webb going forward.

This is a huge update for the Giants from an MLB insider, and should have their fanbase on high alert. This team trading away players makes sense, but Webb has been off-limits. That is no longer the case, as he's now seemingly available for trade.
